questions.question: On a number line marked in whole units from −8 to 8, point A sits at −5 and point B sits at −2. On this line, numbers get smaller as you move to the left. Which statement is true?
options: −5 < −2, because −5 sits farther to the left
−5 = −2, because both points sit on the left side of 0
−5 > −2, because 5 is bigger than 2
−2 < −5, because −2 is closer to 0
questions.explain: On a number line the number farther LEFT is always the smaller one, so −5 < −2. The common trap is comparing 5 and 2 and forgetting that a bigger negative digit means farther left, which means smaller.

questions.question: A number line is marked in whole units with 0 in the middle. A frog starts at 0 and hops 6 equal units to the left, landing on −6. The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0 but on the other side of 0. Which number is the opposite of −6?
options: −6, because the opposite of a negative number is still negative
6, which is 6 units to the right of 0
0, because 0 is the middle of the number line
−12, because you hop 6 more units to the left
questions.explain: To find an opposite, keep the same distance from 0 but switch sides, so −6 becomes 6. The common trap is hopping farther left instead of crossing to the other side of 0.

questions.question: On a number line marked in whole units from −10 to 10, marker P is at −7, marker Q is at 3, and marker R is at −1. Reading the line from left to right lists the numbers from least to greatest. Which order is correct?
questions.explain: Walk the number line from left to right: −7 comes first, then −1, then 3. The common trap is putting −1 before −7 because 1 is smaller than 7, but −7 is farther left, so it is the least.

questions.question: On a number line marked in whole units from −10 to 10, Sofia's counter sits at −9 and Ben's counter sits at 6. Distance from 0 means how many units away the counter is. Which statement is true?
options: Ben's counter is farther from 0, and 6 is the greater number
Both counters are the same distance from 0, so the two numbers are equal
Sofia's counter is farther from 0, so −9 is the greater number
Sofia's counter is farther from 0, but 6 is the greater number
questions.explain: Distance from 0 and value are two different things: −9 is 9 units away and 6 is only 6 units away, but 6 sits to the right of −9, so 6 is greater. The common trap is thinking farther from 0 means greater.

questions.question: Order these integers from greatest to least: −3, −11, 0, −7.
questions.explain: Greatest to least means going right to left on the number line: 0, then −3, then −7, then −11. The common trap is treating −11 as the biggest negative because 11 is a big number, but −11 is the farthest left, so it is the least.

questions.question: Which symbol makes this statement true?  −12 ___ −15
options: Neither > nor < works, because two negative numbers cannot be compared
questions.explain: −12 sits to the right of −15 on the number line, so −12 > −15. The common trap is comparing 12 and 15 and choosing the less-than sign, but with negatives the smaller digit is the number closer to 0, and closer to 0 means greater.

questions.question: Let p be the opposite of −8. Which statement about p is true?
options: p = 8 and p < −8
p = −8, because the opposite of a negative number stays negative
p = 8 and p > −8
p = 0, because −8 and its opposite cancel each other out
questions.explain: The opposite of −8 is 8, the same 8 units from 0 but on the right side, and any positive number is greater than any negative number, so 8 > −8. The common trap is saying 8 is smaller because 8 and −8 look the same size.

questions.question: Four students check their lunch-card balances after fees: Ava −$18, Noah −$25, Liam $0, Mia −$6. The app sorts the balances from least to greatest. Which list is correct?
questions.explain: Least means the deepest debt, so start at −$25, then −$18, then −$6, then $0. The common trap is listing −$6 first because 6 is the smallest number of dollars, but owing $6 is better than owing $25, so −$6 is the greater balance.

questions.question: Morning temperatures in Prince George were: Monday −6 °C, Tuesday −11 °C, Wednesday 2 °C, Thursday −4 °C. Jo lists the days from coldest to warmest, then writes the opposite of the coldest temperature. Which line is completely correct?
options: Tue, Mon, Thu, Wed; opposite is 11
Thu, Mon, Tue, Wed; opposite is 4
Tue, Mon, Thu, Wed; opposite is −11
Wed, Thu, Mon, Tue; opposite is −2
questions.explain: Coldest is farthest left on the number line, so −11, −6, −4, 2, and the opposite of −11 is 11 because an opposite switches sides of 0 but keeps the distance. The common trap is calling −4 the coldest because 4 is the smallest digit.

questions.question: Jasper says: 'On my quiz I wrote −7 > −2, because 7 is greater than 2.' Which reply corrects Jasper best?
options: Jasper is right; with negative numbers the bigger digit always makes the bigger number.
Jasper is wrong; −7 is 7 units left of 0 and −2 is only 2 units left, so −7 < −2.
Jasper is wrong; −7 is greater than −2, but only because −7 is farther from 0.
Jasper is right about the size, but he should write −7 = −2 since both are negative.
questions.explain: For negative numbers, a bigger distance from 0 puts you farther LEFT, which makes the number smaller, so −7 < −2. The common trap is ignoring the negative signs and comparing 7 and 2 as if they were counts.

questions.question: A diver near Nanaimo is 14 m below sea level, written as −14 m. A drone hovers at the elevation that is the opposite of the diver's elevation. A few minutes later the diver rises to −9 m. Which statement is true?
options: The drone is at −14 m, and the diver's new depth −9 m is less than −14 m.
The drone is at 14 m, and the diver's new depth −9 m is less than −14 m, because 9 is smaller than 14.
The drone is at 14 m, and the diver's new depth −9 m is greater than −14 m.
The drone is at 0 m, and −9 m is equal in value to −14 m.
questions.explain: The opposite of −14 is 14, the same distance from sea level but above it, and rising from −14 m to −9 m moves closer to 0, so −9 > −14. The common trap is comparing 9 and 14 and deciding −9 is the lower elevation.

questions.question: Four players on a Kamloops hockey team have these plus-minus numbers: Ella −3, Tom +2, Riya −8, Sam −5. The coach posts the players in order from greatest to least. Which player is second on the coach's list?
options: Tom
Sam
Riya
Ella
questions.explain: Greatest to least is 2, −3, −5, −8, so Tom is first and Ella is second. The common trap is ranking −8 right after 2 because 8 is the biggest digit, but −8 is the farthest left, so it is the least of the four.
